Here's an attempt at a PromQL query, but note that it would require appropriate time-series data to work correctly.

The current average request duration for the past 5 minutes:
```promql
avg_over_time(metric_name_request_duration{client="ts-security-service", method="GET", path="/api/v1/securityservice/securityConfigs/{accountId}", status_code=~"2.."}[5m])
```

The corresponding average request duration for the same period last week:
```promql
avg_over_time(metric_name_request_duration{client="ts-security-service", method="GET", path="/api/v1/securityservice/securityConfigs/{accountId}", status_code=~"2.."}[7d - 5m:5m])
```

Now, calculating the difference between these two:
```promql
(current_average - last_week_average)
```

```promql
(
  kube_statefulset_status_replicas_ready{statefulset="tsdb-mysql"}
  /
  kube_statefulset_status_replicas_current{statefulset="tsdb-mysql"}
) * 100
```
